32d1860.summary: Coroutine body of BattleManager.StartBattlePhase. Runs after mulligan: replay fast-forward, boss/skull/campaign intro animations, hero intro voice lines, applies starting enchantments one by one, adds extra hand cards, shows chat/cemetery, waits for the action queue to drain, then starts the first turn.
comments: state 0: first entry. Replays start playing, and a replay that resumes mid-match queues its earlier actions
replay resumes from a later action: pause and feed the already-recorded actions back in
boss match: play the boss intro and wait 3 seconds (resume at state 1)
state 1 resume: boss intro done, fall through to the skull check
skull match: play the skull intro, wait 3 seconds (resume at state 2)
campaign boss match: play its intro, wait 3 seconds (resume at state 3)
state 2 resume: skull intro done, go on to the campaign boss check
intro messages: a campaign post-mulligan script replaces the normal hero intro lines
mark the match as properly started and in battle; hide the mulligan wait text
normal matches without environmental effects: the second player gets the extra 'goes second' card in deck
apply starting enchantments (player first, one per 0.2s step via state 4/5/6)
player enchantments done: now the enemy's enchantments, triggered instantly in a loop
give each side its extra starting hand card, if the hero has one set (first player, then second)
non-tutorial matches show the chat button and the cemetery view
later states: 4 = enchantment step delay, 5 = trigger the player's enchantment and show it, 6 = next one, 7 = queue wait
state 6: advance to the next player enchantment, then loop back to the check at LAB_032d1cf0
wait until all queued board actions are finished (retry every short delay, state 7)
queue empty: remove the dark shade, set the starting hands up and start the first turn coroutine

32d20b8.summary: IEnumerator.Reset for the StartBattlePhase coroutine; always throws NotSupportedException as for all compiler-generated iterators.

32d2124.summary: Coroutine body of BattleManager.StartBattleSequence. Fades out the loading screen, plays the camera intro, creates tutorial/campaign starting troops, runs pre-mulligan scripted actions if any, then starts the mulligan (or the tutorial start sequence).
comments: state 2: the campaign pre-mulligan script finished, go to the mulligan
state 1: the tutorial pre-mulligan script finished, check for a campaign one next
state 0: fade the loading screen and play the camera intro
tutorial and campaign matches begin with scripted starting troops already on the board
tutorial pre-mulligan script: run it and wait for it to finish (state 1)
campaign pre-mulligan script: run it and wait for it to finish (state 2)
tutorial goes straight into its own start sequence; every other match begins the mulligan

32d28f0.summary: Coroutine body of BattleManager.TutorialStartSequence. Waits briefly, lands the enemy then player hero into the field, sets up camera zoom, plays each pre-mulligan scripted tutorial action with its waits, updates deck displays, shows the HUD and starts the battle phase.
comments: states 0-3: short waits then the enemy hero lands into the field
state 0: log and wait for outer delay
state 1: wait about 0.6 seconds
state 2: show the enemy hero and start its landing animation
state 3: wait about 0.8 seconds before the player hero lands
states 4-5: player hero lands, then camera and tutorial script setup
state 4: show the player hero and start its landing animation
state 5: set up camera zoom (no wait when combat auto-zoom is on), then get the tutorial stage's script list
start iterating the scripted actions; the decompiler shows the list enumerator through raw offsets
loop head: take the next scripted action or finish
all actions done: refresh deck displays, show the HUD and hand over to the battle phase
next action: wait its 'wait before' time (can be skipped by the player), then run it in state 6
state 6 (decompiler reads it from the wrong variable): execute the action and wait for its sound or default chat time
state 7: wait the action's 'wait after' time
state 8: close chat boxes if the player skipped, clear the skip flag and loop to the next action
common exit; the unwind code that follows is the try/finally for the enumerator

32d314c.summary: IEnumerator.Reset for the TutorialStartSequence coroutine; always throws NotSupportedException.

32d31b8.summary: Coroutine body of BattleManager.WaitOpponentLastActions. While the opponent is disconnected it keeps waiting in 2-second steps (up to a budget of 12 seconds) for their final actions; then, if still in battle, clears the opponent's claim of match finished and shows the disconnection popup.
comments: state 1: resumed after a 2-second wait
state 0: start with a 12 second budget (0x41480000 is 12.0f)
still waiting for the opponent's last actions and budget left: log, wait 2s and reduce the budget
wait over: if the match is still on, reset the opponent-finished claim and show the disconnect popup
